thread_a.role: TCP backlog/receive path reads receive-buffer limit locklessly

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(sk_rcvbuf)]) from thread_a (the lockless receive/backlog limit check must not be torn by a concurrent write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the setsockopt/autotune writers update sk_rcvbuf under the socket lock, but the backlog/rmem-schedule reader runs from softirq/IRQ and reads sk_rcvbuf without that lock; the two accesses share no lock, so no serialize(g) establishes the single-access atomicity the reader assumes
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write to the limit field -> data race (store-tearing / torn read)

fix_maps_to: patch wraps the sk_rcvbuf writers in WRITE_ONCE and the lockless readers in READ_ONCE -> makes the conflicting single access atomic; a tearing annotation, not a serialize/order/counts guarantee
recall_risk_notes: Object and sites are in the static surface and the category maps to atomic(single access)=data_race, but the read is a best-effort receive-memory admission threshold that tolerates a stale value. The read carries no order intent beyond no-tearing and there is no semantic guard, so the LLM is likely to adjudicate it benign and reject (precision pressure); only a pure-syntactic-race detector would fire. The fix is annotation-only and does not map onto serialize/order/counts.
